# ContinuousReader

> A native multiplatform reading app for macOS, iPadOS, and iPhone. One codebase, three platform-adapted experiences. Built in Swift and SwiftUI.

ContinuousReader is an independent reading app by Oleksii Koshkin. It reads EPUB (fixed-layout included), FB2, MOBI, AZW3, Markdown, HTML, TXT, RTF, PDF (as text or as pages), comics and manga in CBZ and CBR, and — on Mac — DOC/DOCX files (and their ZIP variants). The core value proposition is seamless reading position sync across all Apple devices via iCloud.

## Five readers, one engine

One picture explains the family: JustReader is the nightstand, PlainReader is the bookshelf, ContinuousReader is the whole library. WebReader and NanoReader take the family's reader beyond Apple.

- **ContinuousReader** ($19.99, one-time) — full reading workspace: library with folders and global full-text search, iCloud sync, OPDS catalogs with watchers, mass import, reading statistics
- **PlainReader** ($6.99, one-time) — a long shelf in named, coloured categories that fold away, each book in its own place with its own position; no collection to manage. Tags, a rating and several colours per book, ten facets (category, author, series, genre, colour, tag, language, recent…), conditions with and / or / not, OPDS browser, a searchable history
- **JustReader** (free) — three active books; the closed ones go to a history of ten and load again in one tap. Books from a link. The same engine, typography, themes, translation and Read Aloud

Beyond Apple:

- **WebReader** (free, https://read.continuousreader.app) — the same page engine in any modern browser, on any system. Three active books; EPUB, FB2, MOBI, AZW3, PDF, CBZ, Markdown, TXT and HTML (and their ZIPs); palettes, typefaces, one to four columns, paper and borders; eight interface languages; installable and offline. Books are read on the device and never uploaded.
- **NanoReader** (free, beta; https://continuousreader.app/nanoreader.html) — JustReader for Windows, Linux and Mac as a program of its own: three active books and a history, marks in seven colours, notes and a comment on the book, export to Markdown, CSV, JSON and RIS (Zotero), a reading journal and statistics, contents and search in a window of their own, day, Twilight and night.

The three Apple apps share the ReaderCore engine (local Swift Package), so the reading experience — themes, typography, navigation modes, translation, Read Aloud, bookmarks, per-book notes, reading statistics and the Book Card — is the same in all of them. What differs is how much collection management sits on top.

## Key features

### Reading engine
- WKWebView-based renderer with PositionTracker.js for precise position tracking
- Three navigation modes: continuous scroll, single page, two-page spread (Mac, iPad in landscape)
- 9 system fonts (serif, sans, monospace), full typography control
- Day & Night mode (automatic theme switching based on system appearance)
- Reading position survives font changes, window resizes, device switches, mode switches

### Translation
- Apple Translation framework (on-device, nothing leaves the device)
- Non-disruptive inline panel, auto-translate mode
- Translation statistics and history tracking (optional)

### Voice Reader (Read Aloud)
- Text-to-speech with real-time word highlighting
- Adjustable rate, pitch, volume
- Seamless handoff between reading and listening (same position)

### Library (ContinuousReader only; PlainReader has a categorised shelf instead)
- Three view modes: list, cards (continuous size slider), table (native on Mac)
- Nested virtual folders, several colours per book (7), tags and a rating, genres, Trash with soft delete
- Ten facets in the sidebar (folders, recent, authors, co-authors, series, genres, colours, languages, tags, rating) and conditions built of several picks with and / or / not
- A reading filter (not started, reading, finished) wherever you are; a System interface on Mac and iPad (split view, inspector)
- OPDS catalog browser with shortcuts and watchers (watchers diff feeds against the library and flag books you don't own yet)
- Mass import walking folder trees, deduplicating, and replicating the source structure as folders (Mac)
- Book Card with tabs (Cover/Images/Info/Notes/Bookmarks/Stats) — shared by all three apps; only ContinuousReader can edit a book's own details
- Global search across the full text of every book in the library, jumping straight to the hit
- Interface depth (Flat / Standard / Deep) and an accent colour that reaches every window and sheet
- Rich text notes editor per book
- Reading statistics dashboard + shareable HTML reports
- Self-contained library folder — copy it anywhere for a backup; custom library location (Mac)

### iCloud sync (ContinuousReader only)
- Reading positions sync in real time while reading (with an iCloud KV Store backup); bookmarks, notes, library metadata via iCloud KV Store
- Book files via iCloud Drive
- Master/slave model for concurrent reading (one device owns position per book)
- Works with free iCloud tier for reading state; file sync uses iCloud Drive storage
- Sync panel reachable by tapping the cloud status badge — shows transport state, library stats (books / downloaded / size with on-demand exact disk scan), and Apple-Settings-style list of connected devices with last-activity timestamps. Foreground-only heartbeat (no fake "online" from a backgrounded Mac or locked iPhone). Forget a peer device via context menu (Mac) or swipe (iPhone).

### Platform adaptations
- **Mac**: keyboard shortcuts (F1-F12), panels that dock to any edge, float or pin, island design, drag-and-drop, two-page spread
- **iPad**: swipe gestures, native sheets, external keyboard support
- **iPhone**: one-hand-friendly, bottom tap zones, compact layouts, notch/Dynamic Island-aware fullscreen

## Technical details

- **Stack**: Swift, SwiftUI, WKWebView, SwiftData
- **Minimum OS**: iOS 17.0, macOS 14.0
- **Storage**: SwiftData (local), iCloud KV Store + iCloud Drive (sync)
- **Book storage**: Clean HTML files on disk with readable slug-based folder names
- **Shipped version**: 1.9 "Painted Lady" (November 2026) for ContinuousReader, JustReader and PlainReader — the number tracks the shared engine generation, not each app
- **Release highlights** (what changed in 1.9, with pictures): https://continuousreader.app/whats-new.html
- **1.8 highlights**: https://continuousreader.app/whats-new-1-8.html
- **1.7 highlights**: https://continuousreader.app/whats-new-1-7.html
- **1.6 highlights**: https://continuousreader.app/whats-new-1-6.html
- **1.5 highlights**: https://continuousreader.app/whats-new-1-5.html
- **Privacy**: The apps have no analytics, telemetry or tracking. This website and WebReader count visits (Cloudflare Web Analytics, no cookies). Translation is on-device.
- **Localization**: English + Russian, Ukrainian, Spanish, French, German (1000+ keys)
- **Bundle IDs**: com.lexey111.ContinuousReader, com.lexey111.PlainReader, com.lexey111.JustReader

## Formats supported

EPUB (fixed-layout EPUB reads as pages), FB2, FB2.ZIP, MOBI, AZW3 (Kindle without DRM), Markdown, HTML, TXT, RTF, PDF (text extraction with a preview wizard, or pages as pictures), CBZ and CBR (comics and manga, right to left in spreads), DOC/DOCX (Mac only), and ZIP variants of HTML/TXT/RTF/DOC. An archive of several books opens a chooser with a folder tree and a preview.
Footnote extraction from EPUB and FB2. Chapter extraction. Cover detection. Encoding auto-detection, Chinese (GB18030, Big5) and Japanese (Shift_JIS, EUC-JP, Aozora Bunko markup, furigana) included. Interface in English, Russian, Ukrainian, Spanish, French, German, Simplified Chinese and Japanese.
